decision.reason: The existing full-RC parent observes a 40 dB input-amplitude blocker only 25 MHz from the desired RF tone. A normal Wi-Fi RF preselector is useful for out-of-band energy but cannot be credited with this adjacent-channel separation while retaining a wide 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi passband.
decision.external_rf_preselector_role: required_later_for_antenna, out-of-band, image, package, and matching control; not the credited 25 MHz channel-selection mechanism
decision.external_if_filter_role: optional later board-level relief path only after a measured network and a die/package port boundary are selected

converter_requirements.notes: These are deliberately conservative architectural requirements derived from the current two-tone PEX output, not an implemented ADC specification or a GF180 feasibility claim. The first physical converter leaf is a 0.25 V differential-peak, 320 MS/s sampled-input interface against a declared 5 pF per-leg future CDAC load and 0.25-LSB settling allocation; it must pass full-RC PEX before an ADC topology is promoted.

digital_filter_requirements.notes: A later fixed-point filter, clock plan, group-delay budget, and modulation/EVM verification must replace this scalar tone requirement.

required_next_implementations: matched transmission-gate differential IF sampling interface with complementary, overlap-controlled clocks, after the physically closed NMOS-only baseline was rejected
12-ENOB-or-better 320 MS/s-or-faster converter evidence across its own declared environment
digital channel-filter response, fixed-point error, and clock-jitter evidence
analog blocker compression, noise, LO spur, and IF/baseband coupling evidence
measured/vendor antenna, package, matching, and preselector networks at explicit ports
